exposure: personal factors (occupation, years of experience, hours worked)
systemic factors (annual number of births in current workplace, level of care of current workplace)
outcome: risk perception of obstetric healthcare professionals
willingness to intervene in obstetric settings
cohort: The participants were obstetric healthcare professionals, including midwives and obstetricians, who completed an online survey.
finding: Midwives exhibited a significantly lower risk perception than obstetricians, and factors such as professional qualification, occupation, hours worked, workplace acuity level, and risk perception itself significantly influenced obstetric healthcare professionals' willingness to intervene.
